name: Weekly rollup dashboard refresh
prompt:
Rebuild Riley's weekly rollup dashboard. This runs unattended every weekday morning — do not ask clarifying questions, just produce the updated dashboard.

STEP 1 — Read the current dashboard to reuse its design.
Call mcp__remote-devices__list_artifacts and find the artifact with id "weekly-rollup". Stage its current HTML with mcp__remote-devices__device_stage_files using artifact_ids: ["weekly-rollup"], then read the staged file. That HTML is the template: keep its structure, CSS, palette, light/dark handling and section layout EXACTLY as-is. You are only replacing the data inside it and the header timestamps. If the artifact can't be staged (desktop offline or unsupported), rebuild the page from the layout described in step 3 instead.

STEP 2 — Pull fresh data. Determine today's date and the current Monday–Sunday week in America/Vancouver first (use bash `TZ=America/Vancouver date`). Then:
- Google Calendar (mcp__Google_Calendar__list_events): all events from this week's Monday 00:00 to next Monday 00:00, timeZone America/Vancouver, orderBy startTime, pageSize 100.
- Gmail (mcp__Gmail__search_threads): run BOTH `in:inbox is:unread newer_than:10d` and `in:inbox newer_than:7d -category:promotions`, pageSize 30 each. Judge which threads (if any) are actually waiting on a reply from Riley — a human wrote to him and he hasn't answered. Receipts, reservation confirmations, newsletters and promotions are never "needs a reply".
- Notion: mcp__Notion__notion-query-data-sources in view mode on view_url "view://9fbdc4ff-62c6-4621-b4f8-fe29e233a8c8" (the "My Tasks" list) for open tasks; and in sql mode on data_source_urls ["collection://1cb89b61-fba6-8110-ad2d-000bbd33b6dc"] with query: SELECT "Title", "date:Date:start" AS due, url FROM "collection://1cb89b61-fba6-8110-ad2d-000bbd33b6dc" WHERE "Completed" IS NULL OR "Completed" = '__NO__' ORDER BY due ASC LIMIT 50 — that's the Task Manager → Tasks database. Also get reading-library counts: sql mode on ["collection://e74a31d5-1dae-4840-aa52-a6401ef14dac"] with SELECT "Status", COUNT(*) as n FROM "collection://e74a31d5-1dae-4840-aa52-a6401ef14dac" GROUP BY "Status". And call mcp__Notion__notion-list-recent-pages (limit 25) to see what he's been in lately.
- Google Drive (mcp__Google_Drive__list_recent_files): orderBy lastModified, pageSize 20, excludeContentSnippets true.

STEP 3 — Rewrite the page with the new data. Sections, in order:
1. Header: "Weekly rollup" eyebrow, the week's date range as the h1, a subline with the rebuild timestamp and the next refresh time, and the source chips (Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, Google Drive, and a muted "Google Tasks — no connector" chip).
2. Four stat tiles: commitments left this week; threads needing a reply; open Notion tasks; Drive files touched in the last 7 days.
3. "The week ahead" — one row per remaining day of the week with its events, times in 12-hour Pacific. Recurring/routine items (the daily 7:30am "Give Bella Drugs", the weekly FreshPrep reminder) are styled in the recessive/grey treatment; real commitments get the blue bar. A final greyed "Already" row lists what's already happened earlier this week.
4. Two-column: "Inbox" (whether anything is owed, then the notable recent threads with UNREAD/READ badges) and "Notion" (open task count, the reading-library meter with its three segments and counts, and a sentence on the most recent Notion activity and its date).
5. "Quiet / stalled" — items that have gone untouched and plausibly shouldn't have: files with a deadline implied by their name, shared docs opened once and dropped, long gaps in activity. Each with an age in days. Be honest and specific; if nothing is stalled, say so plainly rather than padding the list.
6. Footer: the "How this stays current" note (snapshot rebuilt each weekday 7:00 AM Pacific) and the "Google Tasks isn't wired in" note.

Accuracy rules: every item on the page must come from a tool response in this run. Never carry forward an item from the previous version of the page that today's data doesn't support, and never invent, estimate or round a count. If a service errors, show that section with an honest "couldn't reach <service> this morning" state instead of stale or made-up data. Empty is a fine answer — a quiet week should look quiet.

STEP 4 — Ship it. Write the complete self-contained HTML (inline CSS, no external requests, no localStorage) to a file, call SendUserFile on it, then call mcp__remote-devices__update_artifact with id "weekly-rollup", that file_uuid, and a short update_summary. If update_artifact fails because the desktop isn't connected, that's fine — the SendUserFile delivery is enough; note it in your reply.

Keep your final message to two sentences: what changed since the last rebuild, and anything that genuinely needs Riley's attention.
